parts.title: Part A
parts.instructions: Escucha la conversación y elige la respuesta que mejor responde a la pregunta. Suena una sola vez.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: Are you coming to the seminar this afternoon?

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: I wish I could, but I have a lab at three.

questions.stem: What does the woman mean?
options: She does not know about the seminar.
questions.explanation: «I wish I could» siempre significa que no puede. Es la expresión más repetida de esta parte.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Did you manage to finish the assignment?

script.speaker: Man
script.text: Let us just say I will be asking for an extension.

questions.stem: What does the man imply?
options: He does not need an extension.
questions.explanation: Respuesta indirecta. Pedir prórroga implica que no terminó.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: The library closes at nine tonight, does it not?

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Actually, they moved it up to seven during exams.

questions.stem: What does the woman say about the library?
questions.explanation: «Moved it up» aquí significa adelantar la hora. Cierra antes.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: How was your presentation?

script.speaker: Man
script.text: I could not have asked for a better audience.

questions.stem: What does the man mean?
questions.explanation: «Could not have asked for a better X» es un elogio, no una queja.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: Do you know where Professor Hall is?

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Not that I know of, but try the third floor.

questions.stem: What does the woman mean?
options: She does not know where he is.
He is on the third floor.
questions.explanation: «Not that I know of» = no lo sé. La sugerencia es solo una posibilidad.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Should we take the bus or walk?

script.speaker: Man
script.text: It is only ten minutes on foot.

questions.stem: What does the man suggest?
questions.explanation: Da un argumento a favor de ir caminando sin decirlo directamente.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: I heard the deadline was extended.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: That is news to me.

questions.stem: What does the woman mean?
questions.explanation: «That is news to me» = no lo sabía. No implica que sea falso.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Are you free to meet on Friday?

script.speaker: Man
script.text: Friday is tight, but Monday works.

questions.stem: What does the man propose?
questions.explanation: «Tight» = complicado. Ofrece la alternativa.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: This chapter is impossible.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: You can say that again.

questions.stem: What does the woman mean?
options: She wants him to repeat it.
questions.explanation: «You can say that again» es acuerdo enfático, no una petición literal.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Did you remember to send the form?

script.speaker: Man
script.text: It completely slipped my mind.

questions.stem: What does the man mean?
questions.explanation: «Slip one's mind» = olvidarse.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: Is the cafeteria still serving lunch?

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: You just missed it.

questions.stem: What does the woman mean?
questions.explanation: «You just missed it» = acabas de perdértelo.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: How do you like the new dormitory?

script.speaker: Man
script.text: It grows on you.

questions.stem: What does the man mean?
options: He disliked it at first but likes it now.
questions.explanation: «It grows on you» = le vas tomando el gusto con el tiempo.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: Do you think we should call the professor?

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: I would hold off until tomorrow.

questions.stem: What does the woman advise?
questions.explanation: «Hold off» = esperar, posponer.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: The registration fee went up again.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: Tell me about it.

questions.stem: What does the man mean?
questions.explanation: «Tell me about it» dicho así es acuerdo con hartazgo, no una petición de información.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: Are you taking Statistics next term?

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: I am still on the fence.

questions.stem: What does the woman mean?
options: She has decided to take it.
questions.explanation: «On the fence» = indeciso.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Can you help me move on Saturday?

script.speaker: Man
script.text: Count me in.

questions.stem: What does the man mean?
questions.explanation: «Count me in» = cuenta conmigo.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: The lecture was three hours long.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: How did you sit through that?

questions.stem: What does the woman imply?
options: The lecture was hard to endure.
She wants to attend next time.
questions.explanation: «Sit through» implica aguantar algo pesado.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Did the experiment work?

script.speaker: Man
script.text: Back to the drawing board.

questions.stem: What does the man mean?
options: It failed and must be redone.
questions.explanation: «Back to the drawing board» = a empezar de cero.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: Should I apply for the scholarship?

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: You have nothing to lose.

questions.stem: What does the woman advise?
questions.explanation: «Nothing to lose» anima a intentarlo.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Is Daniel joining us for dinner?

script.speaker: Man
script.text: He said he would rather stay in.

questions.stem: What will Daniel do?
questions.explanation: «Would rather stay in» = prefiere quedarse en casa.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: How much did the textbook cost?

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: It cost an arm and a leg.

questions.stem: What does the woman mean?
questions.explanation: «An arm and a leg» = carísimo.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Did you talk to the advisor about changing majors?

script.speaker: Man
script.text: I have been putting it off.

questions.stem: What does the man mean?
questions.explanation: «Put off» = aplazar.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: The results contradict last year's study.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: That is exactly what caught my eye.

questions.stem: What does the woman mean?
questions.explanation: «Catch one's eye» = llamar la atención.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Will the field trip be cancelled?

script.speaker: Man
script.text: It is up in the air.

questions.stem: What does the man mean?
questions.explanation: «Up in the air» = sin decidir.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: I thought the exam went badly.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: You are being too hard on yourself.

questions.stem: What does the woman mean?
options: She did not take the exam.
He is judging himself too harshly.
questions.explanation: «Be hard on yourself» = ser demasiado severo con uno mismo.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Have you found a roommate yet?

script.speaker: Man
script.text: I am still looking, but it is looking up.

questions.stem: What does the man mean?
questions.explanation: «Looking up» = mejorando.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: Do you want me to explain the theory again?

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: No, it finally clicked.

questions.stem: What does the woman mean?
questions.explanation: «It clicked» = por fin lo entendí.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: The department is hiring two new professors.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: About time.

questions.stem: What does the man mean?
options: He thinks it happened too soon.
questions.explanation: «About time» = ya iba siendo hora.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: Can we push the meeting to four?

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: That works better for me anyway.

questions.stem: What does the woman mean?
questions.explanation: «Works better for me» = le viene mejor.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Are you nervous about the defence?

script.speaker: Man
script.text: I have butterflies, but I am ready.

questions.stem: What does the man mean?
questions.explanation: «Butterflies» (in one's stomach) = nervios. Pero dice que está listo.

parts.title: Part B · Conversación 1
parts.instructions: Escucha la conversación y responde a las preguntas. Suena una sola vez.

script.speaker: Student
script.text: Excuse me, I am trying to register for the seminar on urban history, but the system says the course is full.

script.speaker: Advisor
script.text: Let me check. Yes, it filled up in the first two days. It is unusually popular this term.

script.speaker: Student
script.text: Is there a waiting list?

script.speaker: Advisor
script.text: There is, and you would be number nine. Realistically, about four spots open up each year when people change their schedules.

script.speaker: Student
script.text: So my chances are not great.

script.speaker: Advisor
script.text: Not this term, no. But the same professor teaches a similar course in the spring, and that one rarely fills.

script.speaker: Student
script.text: Would it count for the same requirement?

script.speaker: Advisor
script.text: It would. The content overlaps by about seventy percent. The spring version focuses more on transport networks than on housing.

script.speaker: Student
script.text: That actually suits my thesis better.

script.speaker: Advisor
script.text: Then I would put your name down for spring and skip the waiting list entirely.

questions.stem: Why is the student speaking to the advisor?
options: To register for a full course.
questions.explanation: Lo dice en la primera intervención: intenta inscribirse y el curso está lleno.

questions.stem: What does the advisor say about the waiting list?
options: It is unlikely to reach him.
questions.explanation: Es el número nueve y solo se liberan unas cuatro plazas.

questions.stem: How does the spring course differ?
options: It is taught by another professor.
It focuses more on transport networks.
It does not count for the requirement.
questions.explanation: El mismo profesor, con más peso en redes de transporte.

questions.stem: What does the advisor recommend?
questions.explanation: Aconseja apuntarse a primavera y saltarse la lista de espera.

parts.title: Part B · Conversación 2
parts.instructions: Escucha la conversación y responde a las preguntas. Suena una sola vez.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Did you get the results back from the soil samples?

script.speaker: Man
script.text: I did, and they are strange. The nitrogen levels are three times what we predicted.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Three times? Could the samples have been contaminated?

script.speaker: Man
script.text: That was my first thought, so I ran the control twice. The control came back normal both times.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Then something is genuinely different about that field.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: I checked the land records. It was used for livestock until about fifteen years ago.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: That would explain it. Manure raises nitrogen and it stays in the soil for decades.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: It also means our comparison with the other site is not valid any more.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: We would need a third site with no farming history.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: Which puts us about two months behind.

questions.stem: What is unusual about the results?
options: The nitrogen levels are far higher than predicted.
The results match the prediction exactly.
questions.explanation: Tres veces lo previsto.

questions.stem: Why does the man mention running the control twice?
options: To show the equipment was broken.
To confirm the woman's theory about livestock.
questions.explanation: Fue su primera sospecha y la descartó repitiendo el control.

questions.stem: What explains the high nitrogen levels?
options: The field's history as livestock land.
questions.explanation: El terreno se usó para ganado hasta hace quince años.

questions.stem: What is the consequence for their research?
options: They must repeat all the tests.
They must find a third site, delaying the project.
questions.explanation: Necesitan un tercer sitio sin historial agrícola, unos dos meses de retraso.

parts.title: Part C · Charla 1
parts.instructions: Escucha la charla y responde a las preguntas. Suena una sola vez.

script.speaker: Professor
script.text: Before we begin today's topic, a word about the mid-term. It will cover chapters one through six, not through eight as the syllabus states. I corrected that yesterday.

script.speaker: Professor
script.text: Now, the printing press. We tend to describe it as an invention that spread ideas, which is true but incomplete.

script.speaker: Professor
script.text: What changed more profoundly was not the speed of copying but the stability of the copy. Before print, every manuscript differed slightly from its source, because every copy was made by hand.

script.speaker: Professor
script.text: Errors accumulated across generations of copies. Two scholars in different cities could not be certain they were reading the same text.

script.speaker: Professor
script.text: Print made the identical copy possible. That is what allowed scholars to cite a page number and expect another reader to find the same words there.

script.speaker: Professor
script.text: Modern scholarship depends on that assumption, and it is barely five hundred years old.

questions.stem: What correction does the professor make about the mid-term?
options: It covers fewer chapters than stated.
It covers more chapters than stated.
questions.explanation: Capítulos 1 a 6, no hasta el 8 como decía el programa.

questions.stem: According to the professor, what was the most profound change brought by print?
questions.explanation: Lo dice explícitamente: no la velocidad, sino la estabilidad.

questions.stem: What problem existed with handmade manuscripts?
questions.explanation: Cada copia difería y los errores se acumulaban.

questions.stem: Why does the professor mention citing a page number?
options: To illustrate what identical copies made possible.
questions.explanation: Es el ejemplo de lo que permitió la copia idéntica.

parts.title: Part C · Charla 2
parts.instructions: Escucha la charla y responde a las preguntas. Suena una sola vez.

script.speaker: Guide
script.text: Welcome to the wetland reserve. Before we walk out, three things you should know.

script.speaker: Guide
script.text: First, stay on the boardwalk. The ground either side looks solid and is not. Every year we pull somebody out.

script.speaker: Guide
script.text: Second, the birds you came to see are most active in the first hour after sunrise and the last hour before sunset. At midday you will mostly see insects.

script.speaker: Guide
script.text: Third, this reserve was farmland until 1994. What you are walking through is not preserved wilderness; it is restored wetland.

script.speaker: Guide
script.text: That distinction matters, because visitors often assume restoration is a second-best outcome. In terms of species count, this site now outperforms two of the three natural wetlands in the region.

script.speaker: Guide
script.text: Restoration is slow, but it works. The oldest section took eleven years to reach that point.

questions.stem: Why must visitors stay on the boardwalk?
options: The ground beside it is unsafe.
questions.explanation: Parece firme y no lo es; cada año sacan a alguien.

questions.stem: When are the birds most active?
questions.explanation: La primera hora tras el amanecer y la última antes del ocaso.

questions.stem: What does the guide say about the reserve's history?
questions.explanation: Era terreno agrícola hasta 1994.

questions.stem: What point does the guide make about restoration?
options: It can outperform natural sites over time.
It is too expensive to repeat.
questions.explanation: Supera a dos de los tres humedales naturales de la región en número de especies.

parts.title: Part C · Charla 3
parts.instructions: Escucha el anuncio y responde a las preguntas. Suena una sola vez.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: Attention all students using the west campus laboratories.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: Beginning Monday, access to the building will require the new identification card, not the old one.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: Cards can be collected from the administration office between nine and four on weekdays. Bring your student number and any form of photo identification.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: If you hold a research key for after-hours access, that key remains valid and does not need to be replaced.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: Please note that the office will be closed this Wednesday for staff training, so do not leave it until the last day.

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of the announcement?
options: To explain a change in building access.
questions.explanation: El tema central es la nueva tarjeta para entrar.

questions.stem: What must students bring to collect the card?
options: The old card and a fee.
Their student number and photo identification.
questions.explanation: Lo dice explícitamente.

questions.stem: What does the announcer say about research keys?
options: They work only during office hours.
questions.explanation: Siguen valiendo y no hay que cambiarlas.

questions.stem: Why should students not wait until the last day?
options: The office closes Wednesday for training.
questions.explanation: Cierra el miércoles por formación del personal.

parts.title: Structure
parts.instructions: Elige la palabra o frase que completa correctamente la oración.

questions.stem: The number of applications ______ significantly since the new policy was introduced.
questions.explanation: «The number of» siempre va en singular: has. Distinto de «a number of», que va en plural.

questions.stem: ______ the storm, the ceremony was moved indoors.
questions.explanation: Se necesita una preposición seguida de sustantivo. «Despite of» no existe y «in spite» está incompleto; «although» exige una oración con verbo.

questions.stem: Not until the results were published ______ the extent of the problem.
questions.explanation: Tras un adverbial negativo al principio, el orden se invierte: did + sujeto + verbo base.

questions.stem: The report recommends that each department ______ its budget by March.
questions.explanation: Subjuntivo tras «recommend»: forma base sin -s, aunque el sujeto sea singular.

questions.stem: ______ in the region for over a decade, she knows the terrain better than anyone.
questions.explanation: Cláusula de participio: sustituye a «Since she has worked...». Las otras dejan la oración sin estructura.

questions.stem: The results were far more encouraging than ______.
questions.explanation: Tras «than» va una oración normal. «What» y «as» sobran en esta comparación.

questions.stem: Neither the students nor the instructor ______ aware of the change.
questions.explanation: Con «neither... nor» el verbo concuerda con el sujeto MÁS CERCANO, que aquí es «the instructor», singular.

questions.stem: It was the lack of funding, not the design, ______ caused the delay.
questions.explanation: Oración escindida enfática: «It was X that...». Se usa «that», no «what».

questions.stem: Rarely ______ such a clear correlation between the two variables.
questions.explanation: Inversión obligatoria tras «rarely» al comienzo de la oración.

questions.stem: The equipment ______ to the laboratory last week has not been unpacked.
questions.explanation: Participio pasado en función de adjetivo: «the equipment (that was) delivered». La opción B dejaría dos verbos principales.

questions.stem: Only after the second trial ______ that the method was flawed.
questions.explanation: «Only after» al principio también fuerza la inversión con el auxiliar.

questions.stem: The professor insisted that the deadline ______ extended.
questions.explanation: Subjuntivo tras «insist»: forma base «be», sin conjugar.

questions.stem: Of the two proposals, the second was ______.
questions.explanation: Con solo dos elementos se usa el comparativo con artículo: «the more practical of the two».

questions.stem: ______ the samples had been contaminated was not discovered until much later.
questions.explanation: «That» introduce la oración que hace de sujeto. «What» cambiaría el significado y dejaría la frase incompleta.

questions.stem: Hardly ______ the presentation when the power failed.
questions.explanation: «Hardly... when» exige inversión con el pasado perfecto: had + sujeto + participio.

parts.title: Written Expression
parts.instructions: Señala el fragmento subrayado que NO es correcto.

questions.stem: The report (A) was completed on time, (B) although the committee (C) have decided to (D) postpone the vote.
questions.explanation: «Committee» es un colectivo que en registro de examen va en singular: has decided.

questions.stem: She is one of the few (A) researchers who (B) has published (C) in that field (D) this year.
questions.explanation: El verbo concuerda con «researchers», no con «one»: have published.

questions.stem: The data (A) collected last summer (B) was analysed (C) careful before (D) being published.
questions.explanation: Un verbo se modifica con adverbio: carefully, no careful.

questions.stem: (A) The board reviewed both proposals, (B) but neither of the (C) two solutions (D) are acceptable.
questions.explanation: «Neither of» va en singular: is acceptable.

questions.stem: He has been (A) living in Toronto (B) since (C) five years, and (D) he plans to stay.
questions.explanation: Con una duración se usa «for», no «since».

questions.stem: The study examines (A) how children learn, (B) how adults teach and (C) the memory works (D) in both groups.
questions.explanation: Estructura paralela rota: los tres elementos deberían empezar por «how».

questions.stem: The excavation (A) continued without interruption (B) throughout the week, (C) despite of the (D) heavy rain.
questions.explanation: «Despite» nunca lleva «of». Sería «despite» o «in spite of».

questions.stem: The professor, (A) along with two assistants, (B) were present (C) at the demonstration (D) yesterday.
questions.explanation: «Along with» no cambia el sujeto: sigue siendo «the professor», singular. Debe ser «was».

questions.stem: It is (A) recommended that every applicant (B) submits (C) two references (D) before the deadline.
questions.explanation: Subjuntivo tras «recommend»: submit, sin -s.

questions.stem: The results were (A) more better than (B) those obtained (C) in the previous (D) experiment.
questions.explanation: «More better» no existe. «Better» ya es comparativo.

questions.stem: (A) The technician recorded the data, (B) filed the report and (C) each of the samples (D) were tested three times.
questions.explanation: «Each of» va en singular: was tested.

questions.stem: The theory (A) which she proposed (B) it has been (C) widely accepted (D) since 2010.
questions.explanation: El «it» sobra: el sujeto ya es «the theory» y la relativa no lo repite.

questions.stem: The project (A) was abandoned so quickly (B) that few people (C) understood (D) why there is several reasons behind it.
options: why there is several reasons behind it
questions.explanation: «There are several reasons»: el verbo concuerda con el sujeto pospuesto, que es plural.

questions.stem: (A) Before we entered the laboratory, (B) the supervisor (C) reviewed the safety rules and (D) explained us the procedure.
questions.explanation: «Explain» necesita «to»: explained the procedure to us. Error muy frecuente en hispanohablantes.

questions.stem: (A) The most of the participants (B) reported (C) an improvement (D) within two weeks.
questions.explanation: «Most of the participants», sin artículo delante de «most».

questions.stem: The building, (A) constructed in 1890, (B) has been (C) recently renovated (D) by a local firm last year.
options: by a local firm last year
questions.explanation: «Last year» exige pasado simple, no presente perfecto: «was renovated».

questions.stem: (A) I would have rescheduled the meeting (B) and warned the team (C) about the change (D) if I would have known.
options: I would have rescheduled the meeting
questions.explanation: En la cláusula con «if» del tercer condicional va «had known», nunca «would have known».

questions.stem: The research (A) provides (B) an evidence (C) that the two phenomena (D) are related.
questions.explanation: «Evidence» es incontable: no lleva «an».

questions.stem: Scientists (A) have long suspected (B) that the mineral (C) forms slow (D) under high pressure.
questions.explanation: Adverbio: forms slowly.

questions.stem: (A) Although the sample was small, (B) but the findings (C) were consistent (D) with earlier work.
questions.explanation: «Although» y «but» no se usan juntos. Sobra el «but».

questions.stem: The instrument (A) is capable (B) to measure (C) temperatures (D) below freezing.
questions.explanation: «Capable of measuring». Tras «capable of» va gerundio.

questions.stem: (A) To graduate from the programme, (B) a research project (C) must be completed (D) by every students enrolled.
questions.explanation: «Every» va siempre con singular: every student.

questions.stem: The findings (A) suggest that (B) the population (C) has grown (D) more rapid than expected.
questions.explanation: Adverbio comparativo: more rapidly.

questions.stem: (A) By the time the team arrived, (B) the equipment (C) already failed (D) three times.
options: By the time the team arrived
questions.explanation: «By the time» en pasado exige pasado perfecto: had already failed.

questions.stem: The author (A) discusses about (B) the origins (C) of the tradition (D) in the second chapter.
questions.explanation: «Discuss» es transitivo directo: discusses the origins, sin «about».

parts.title: Texto 1
parts.instructions: Lee el texto y responde a las preguntas.
parts.passage:
The formation of caves in limestone regions depends on a chemical process that is easy to state and slow to observe. Rainwater absorbs carbon dioxide as it falls and more of it as it filters through soil, becoming a weak carbonic acid. Limestone, which is largely calcium carbonate, dissolves in this acid. Over thousands of years, water moving along cracks widens them into passages and eventually into chambers.

What determines the shape of a cave system is therefore not the strength of the water but the pattern of the original cracks. Where the rock is heavily jointed, caves tend to form as networks of interconnected passages. Where a single fracture dominates, the result is often one long tunnel with few branches.

The rate of dissolution is also governed by temperature, though not in the direction most people assume. Cold water holds more dissolved carbon dioxide than warm water, and so is more acidic. Cave formation is consequently more rapid in temperate regions than in the tropics, despite the greater rainfall in tropical areas. This has led to a persistent misconception in older literature, which attributed the abundance of tropical caves to rainfall alone. The abundance is real, but it reflects the extent of exposed limestone rather than the speed of dissolution.

questions.stem: What is the main topic of the passage?
options: The uses of limestone in construction.
How caves form in limestone and what governs their shape.
questions.explanation: Idea principal: el proceso de formación y los factores que la gobiernan.

questions.stem: According to the passage, rainwater becomes acidic because it
questions.explanation: Detalle explícito del primer párrafo.

questions.stem: The word «jointed» in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to
questions.explanation: Vocabulario en contexto: se habla de grietas originales.

questions.stem: What determines whether a cave becomes a network or a single tunnel?
options: The pattern of the original cracks.
questions.explanation: Lo dice literalmente al inicio del segundo párrafo.

questions.stem: Why is cave formation faster in temperate regions?
questions.explanation: El agua fría retiene más CO2 y por tanto es más ácida.

questions.stem: The word «it» in paragraph 1 refers to
questions.explanation: «absorbs carbon dioxide... and more of it»: se refiere al dióxido de carbono.

questions.stem: It can be inferred from paragraph 3 that older literature
options: confused abundance with rate of formation.
was largely correct about tropical caves.
ignored the role of temperature entirely.
was based on temperate regions only.
questions.explanation: Atribuía la abundancia tropical a la lluvia; el texto dice que la abundancia es real pero por otra causa.

questions.stem: The author mentions rainfall in the tropics in order to
options: contrast expectation with the actual cause.

parts.title: Texto 2

parts.passage:
Migratory birds navigate using several systems at once, and the redundancy appears to be deliberate rather than accidental. Experiments in the 1960s established that many species orient themselves by the position of the stars, a capacity that develops in young birds during their first autumn and can be disrupted by raising them under an artificial sky.

Later work identified a second mechanism based on the earth's magnetic field. Birds appear to detect not the polarity of the field, as a compass needle does, but its inclination, that is, the angle at which the field lines meet the ground. This distinction matters, because an inclination compass gives the same reading at both poles and must be recalibrated for birds that cross the equator.

A third system relies on the pattern of polarised light at sunset, which indicates the position of the sun after it has dropped below the horizon.

What has proved difficult to establish is how these systems are ranked when they conflict. Displacement experiments, in which birds are moved hundreds of kilometres before release, suggest that the magnetic system dominates in overcast conditions but yields to celestial cues when the sky is clear. The consensus, such as it is, holds that no single system is primary; rather, birds weight them according to reliability at that moment.

parts.title: Texto 3

parts.passage:
The Bauhaus school operated for only fourteen years and was closed three times, yet its influence on twentieth-century design is difficult to overstate. Founded in Weimar in 1919, it was less a style than a proposal about how objects should be made.

Its central claim was that the separation between fine art and craft was historically recent and artificially maintained. Students were taught in workshops rather than studios, and were expected to work in metal, textiles or wood before specialising. A furniture designer was expected to be able to build the chair.

The visual language commonly associated with the school, that is, flat planes, primary colours and the absence of ornament, emerged relatively late and was never universal among its members. It became dominant partly because it photographed well, and photographs travelled further than buildings.

When the school was closed for the third and final time in 1933, its staff dispersed across Europe and the United States. This dispersal, rather than any organised campaign, is what carried the approach abroad. Within a decade, its former teachers held influential positions in American architecture schools, and the workshop model was widely adopted, though frequently without the political commitments that had accompanied it in Germany.

parts.title: Texto 4
parts.instructions: Lee el texto y responde a las preguntas.
parts.passage:
For most of the twentieth century, economists treated household work as outside the economy. It was not counted in national accounts, and by convention it had no value. The reasoning was practical rather than ideological: there was no transaction, no price and therefore nothing to measure.

The consequences of this convention were not neutral. A country whose citizens grew and cooked their own food appeared poorer than one whose citizens bought identical meals in restaurants. When a service moved from the home to the market, national income rose, though no additional work had been done.

Attempts to correct this have generally used one of two methods. The replacement-cost approach asks what it would cost to hire someone to do the same work. The opportunity-cost approach asks what the person doing it could have earned instead. The two produce strikingly different figures, and the gap is largest for high earners, whose forgone wages are large but whose domestic output is no greater than anyone else's.

Neither method has been adopted in standard accounts, partly for these technical reasons and partly because the resulting figures are politically inconvenient. Estimates that place unpaid household work at between a quarter and a half of measured national output invite questions about who performs it and whether existing arrangements are equitable.

parts.title: Texto 5
parts.instructions: Lee el texto y responde a las preguntas.
parts.passage:
Coral reefs occupy less than one percent of the ocean floor yet support roughly a quarter of all marine species. This concentration has long puzzled biologists, because the waters surrounding reefs are typically poor in nutrients. An ecosystem of that density would normally require a rich supply of them.

The explanation lies in recycling rather than input. Reef organisms retain nutrients within the system to an unusual degree, passing them between coral, algae and the animals that graze on both. The partnership between coral and the algae living inside its tissue is central: the algae supply sugars produced by photosynthesis, and the coral supplies the nitrogen compounds the algae need. Very little escapes.

This efficiency is also the source of the system's fragility. Because the reef depends on an internal cycle rather than on external supply, disruptions propagate quickly. When water temperatures rise beyond a narrow threshold, coral expels its algae, a process known as bleaching. The coral does not die immediately, but without the algae it loses most of its energy supply.

Recovery is possible if temperatures fall within weeks. What has changed in recent decades is not the occurrence of bleaching events, which are natural, but the interval between them, which has shortened to less than the time a reef requires to recover.
